small_guidance:
- The GEMM uses `allow_tf32=False` which forces full FP32 mma and is the main bottleneck on a 1024×8192×8192 problem. Switch to `allow_tf32=True` (the reference uses cuBLAS which uses TF32 on Ampere/Ada by default at this tolerance) — this alone should ~2x the GEMM.
- Add larger autotune configs targeted at this exact shape: `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64, num_warps=8, num_stages=3/4` and `BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=256, BLOCK_K=64` (M=1024 is small, so favor wider N tiles and modest M). Also try `num_stages=4` with `BLOCK_K=64` to overlap K-loop loads.
- Drop in-loop boundary masks since M=1024, N=8192, K=8192 are all clean multiples of typical tiles — unconditional `tl.load` (or load once outside the loop with `tl.multiple_of`/`tl.max_contiguous` hints) removes per-iter compare overhead.
large_guidance:
- Fuse the BN epilogue into the GEMM kernel for the eval path, and for training compute per-column sum and sum-of-squares directly inside the GEMM kernel via `atomic_add` into two (N,) accumulators — eliminates the separate two-pass `bn_stats_kernel` (which re-reads the full (M,N) tensor twice) and the separate `bn_apply_kernel`. Then a tiny (N,) kernel finalizes mean/invstd, and a second pass applies (scale, shift). For M=1024 this can collapse three full M×N memory traversals into roughly one.
- Alternatively, structure as a "split-K-free" persistent GEMM that writes the GEMM+scale output and simultaneously accumulates column stats in shared memory then atomically reduces per-tile to global — avoids the extra read pass while keeping `tl.dot` throughput.
- Pre-transpose W to (K, N) contiguous once in `__init__` so the inner B load is fully contiguous along N rather than strided (`stride_bn=K`), which currently hurts L2/coalescing on the B operand.
